clue.text: They may be seen at the courts, practising

definitions.text: They may be seen at the courts, practising

parts.words: They may be seen at the courts, practising
parts.note: a sporting picture of players at tennis courts, really lawyers who practise law in the law courts

explanation.surface: Tennis players are spotted knocking up at the courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Courts' and 'practising' suggest tennis, but the courts are law courts and practising means following a legal profession.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the legal profession who argue cases are said to practise at the bar in court.

clue.text: Song and a soaring tune

indicators.note: soaring means rising, so in this down answer the tune word is read upwards

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A song with a melody that climbs high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' reverses AIR to RIA in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo song in an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: One way of underlining decision

definitions.meaning: drawing lines, as on lined paper, is one way to underline
a judgment given by a court or official

explanation.surface: A method of emphasising a final judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling means drawing straight lines, and also an authoritative decision.

clue.text: Power switch at mains

indicators.note: switch means the letters are exchanged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An electrical power switch located at the mains supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' and 'switch' suggest electricity; power is endurance here and 'switch' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical staying power or endurance.

clue.text: Prepare to put out with rising tide

indicators.note: rising means the word is read upwards in this down answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sailors get ready to set out on the incoming tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' suggests sailing, but it means publish.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare text for publication, putting it out.

clue.text: Without speaking, communicates: 'Exceptional spades'

parts.note: signal as an adjective means notable or exceptional
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: A silent bridge player conveys a bid of exceptional spades.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGNAL as an adjective means remarkable, as in 'a signal success'.
explanation.definitionFit: To gesture or make signs is to convey messages without words.

clue.text: Perfect demonstration of being impervious to noise

parts.note: sound means in perfect condition
proof is a demonstration of truth

explanation.surface: A flawless test shows a room is insulated against noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulated so that no noise can pass through.

clue.text: Business, he thinks, should not be a matter of duty

definitions.text: Business, he thinks, should not be a matter of duty

parts.words: Business, he thinks, should not be a matter of duty
parts.note: duty means customs tax: this person believes commerce should be tariff-free, not a moral obligation

explanation.surface: Someone thinks working should not be a moral obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' reads as obligation but means customs duty on imports.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate of commerce between nations without tariffs or customs charges.

clue.text: Growl when shaver is returned with middle part missing

indicators.note: the central letter of the turned word is dropped, leaving its two ends joined
returned means the word for the shaver is read backwards

parts.note: a razor is a shaver

explanation.surface: Someone growls when their electric shaver comes back broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is returned' turns RAZOR into ROZAR; 'with middle part missing' removes its central letter Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep loud animal noise, as from a lion; a growl is a near synonym.

clue.text: A single? Mid off is not clear

indicators.note: off means the letters of the preceding words are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cricket question: is a single run to the mid-off fielder an unclear call?
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket terms mislead: a single is one run and mid-off a fielding position. 'off' is the anagram signal on A SINGLE MID.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives a false or confusing impression is not clear, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Shade of nun seen round a religious establishment

indicators.note: round means the first word's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England, the established religion

explanation.surface: A nun is glimpsed walking around a religious house in the shadows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nun' looks like part of the definition's picture but is taken literally; CE is the Church of England, Britain's established church.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtle gradation or tint in meaning or colour is a shade.

clue.text: Fancy a Lennon song

definitions.meaning: to fancy is to picture something in the mind
the title of John Lennon's best-known solo song of 1971

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a John Lennon track.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to form a mental picture, which is to fancy; it is also the title of a famous Lennon song.

clue.text: Big banker experiments in commercial enterprises

parts.note: a river has banks, so a big river is a big banker: the Indus
tries are attempts or experiments

explanation.surface: A major financier tests new ideas in business ventures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is the crossword trick for a river, which has banks; the Indus is a great Asian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Branches of manufacturing or trade, or businesses generally.

clue.text: As a diplomat he is seen in capitals

definitions.text: As a diplomat he is seen in capitals

parts.words: As a diplomat he is seen in capitals
parts.note: envoys live in foreign capital cities; capitals also hints at capital letters

explanation.surface: A diplomat is posted to capital cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior diplomat representing his country in a foreign capital.

clue.text: Level betting for the first woman to get two points

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
N is north, a compass point
S is south, another compass point

explanation.surface: At the races, a punter's first wife wins two points on an even bet.
explanation.walkthrough: The two points are compass points, North and South.
explanation.definitionFit: Odds where the stake and winnings are equal, even money.

clue.text: It receives indication a doctor is required

definitions.text: It receives indication a doctor is required

parts.words: It receives indication a doctor is required
parts.note: describes the pager carried by hospital doctors that sounds when they are called

explanation.surface: A device or person gets a sign that medical help is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pager that emits a beep to summon its holder, traditionally carried by hospital doctors.

clue.text: Money for being raised hand-to-mouth?

definitions.meaning: a staple food lifted to the mouth, and leavened dough that rises

explanation.surface: Cash for someone living hand to mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hand-to-mouth' suggests poverty, but literally describes eating a staple food.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, and is the food lifted hand to mouth.

clue.text: Declares a piece of poetry interminably

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the poetry word is removed

parts.note: a verse is a piece of poetry

explanation.surface: Someone announces a poem and then recites it endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' cuts the last letter E off VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state positively, a synonym of declare.

clue.text: Experts in digitally recorded evidence

definitions.meaning: dab hands, people who are skilled at something
slang for fingerprints, recorded by the fingers

explanation.surface: Specialists in forensic or computer evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digitally' suggests computers, but it means with the digits, the fingers: fingerprints are known as dabs in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab is an expert (as in dab hand), and fingerprints are dabs in police slang.

clue.text: Cover for American gangster

definitions.meaning: a covering for the head or for a machine
a hoodlum, shortened in US slang

explanation.surface: A front for a US mobster.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood is a head covering, and in American slang a hood is a hoodlum or gangster.

clue.text: Work to make some dough

parts.note: suggests earning money (dough), but describes working bread mixture by hand

explanation.surface: Someone takes a job to earn a bit of cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' as slang for money is the false trail; here it is bread mixture being pressed and folded.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakers press and fold bread mixture with their hands to develop it.

clue.text: High after joints in wild party

indicators.note: after means the word for high comes behind the joints word

parts.note: knees are joints
up means high

explanation.surface: Getting high after smoking joints at a wild party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joints' and 'High' suggest drugs; they are knees and UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, boisterous party with dancing, in British slang.

clue.text: Rodents carry out unusual crime

parts.note: to do is to carry out

indicators.note: unusual means the letters of crime are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Rats commit a strange offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CRIME into RMICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small hibernating rodents that resemble mice.

clue.text: Birds I hide in ship

indicators.note: in means the following pieces are placed inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
a skin is an animal's hide

explanation.surface: A stowaway confesses to hiding aboard a vessel among the birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' reads as a verb (conceal) but is the noun, an animal skin; SS is the steamship prefix on ship names.
explanation.definitionFit: Small yellow-green finches, a kind of songbird.

clue.text: Ruined roof end in need of repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A gable at the end of the roof is wrecked and needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means finished or doomed beyond saving, the same as ruined.

clue.text: Strange noises in Greek/Cypriot union

indicators.note: strange means the letters of noises are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Odd sounds are heard in the politics of Greece and Cyprus.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement for political union of Cyprus with Greece.

clue.text: Organiser of musical group that is on the way

indicators.note: on means the abbreviation is placed after the way word in this across answer

parts.note: a road is a way
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A band's tour manager is travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: IE abbreviates Latin id est; 'on' places it after the road word, as in an across answer one piece follows another.
explanation.definitionFit: A touring band's crew member who sets up and organises their equipment.

clue.text: River that's Polish — or German

parts.note: the river forming the Polish German border, flowing in both countries

explanation.surface: A river belonging to Poland or Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the verb to shine, but it is the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Central European river that marks much of the Germany–Poland border.

clue.text: Be a university lover

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university; that the clue words also spell the answer in a run is a coincidence of this charade

explanation.surface: Be a lover at college.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend or male admirer, a sweetheart.

clue.text: Team results not the main topics of conversation

definitions.text: not the main topics of conversation

parts.note: a side is a sports team
issues are outcomes or results

explanation.surface: The football scores are only small talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Matters of secondary importance in a discussion, peripheral rather than central.

clue.text: Cupid has painful back

indicators.note: back means the word for painful is read in reverse

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: The god of love complains of an aching back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, equivalent to the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Worried speculator transfers shares

indicators.note: worried means the letters of the next word are disturbed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An anxious investor sells off stock.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means distributes in portions, handing out shares to each.
